FitzHugh-Nagumo model

Words: 63
Mathematical biology OurBigBook.com
The FitzHugh-Nagumo model represents an excitable cell by a fast activation variable and a slower recovery variable. A common nondimensional form is V˙=V−V3/3−W+I, W˙=ε(V+a−bW). Its cubic activation response and recovery feedback can produce an excitable resting state or sustained oscillations through bifurcations. Particular reductions and travelling-wave equations can have additional state variables; their signs and parameter conventions must be stated separately.

Epidemic

Words: 47
Mathematical biology OurBigBook.com
An epidemic is a period of growing infection incidence in a population. Compartmental models describe transmission, recovery and depletion or renewal of susceptible hosts. An epidemic invasion threshold concerns growth after a small introduction; a final size relation for an epidemic concerns the total susceptible depletion of a closed outbreak. These are distinct from an endemic equilibrium with continuing transmission.

Metapopulation

Words: 332 Articles: 5
Mathematical biology OurBigBook.com
A metapopulation describes occupied habitat patches with local colonization and extinction. The patch occupancy variable differs from population abundance within a patch.

Globally coupled underdominant metapopulation (u˙i​=sui​(1−ui​)(2ui​−1)+σ(uˉ−ui​))

Words: 195 Articles: 2
Metapopulation OurBigBook.com
This model couples deterministic underdominant allele-frequency dynamics in equal-sized habitats by global migration. Starting with m pure habitats of one allele and N−m of the other preserves two within-class frequencies x,y, reducing the system to x˙=f(x)−σ(1−q)(x−y), y˙​=f(y)+σq(x−y) with q=m/N. Migration is conservative in the mean, but selection need not conserve global allele frequency.

Symmetric underdominant two-cluster equilibrium (x∗​=(1+1−2σ/s​)/2,y∗​=1−x∗​)

Words: 61
Globally coupled underdominant metapopulation OurBigBook.com
With equally many initially pure habitats of each allele, symmetry preserves y=1−x. The heterogeneous equilibrium exists for σ<s/2. Its full-system eigenvalues are −s+3σ in the mean-frequency direction and −s+2σ in the antisymmetric direction, so it attracts general nearby perturbations only for σ<s/3. Exact symmetry can preserve both alleles beyond this robust range; at stronger migration it approaches the unstable uniform midpoint.

Invariant-rectangle criterion for underdominant coexistence (σmax(q,1−q)<s/8)

Words: 80
Globally coupled underdominant metapopulation OurBigBook.com
In the two-class globally coupled underdominant metapopulation, the rectangle 3/4≤x≤1, 0≤y≤1/4 is forward invariant under the displayed bound. On its inner edges, selection points inward with magnitude 3s/32 while outward migration is at most (3/4)σ(1−q) or (3/4)σq; the outer edges also point inward. Thus prescribed initial state (1,0) cannot approach global allele fixation when 0<q<1. Maximizing f(u)/u=s(1−u)(2u−1) gives s/8 at u=3/4, making the bound optimal within this particular symmetric worst-case rectangle argument, not a universal sharp migration threshold.

Levins metapopulation model (p˙​=cp(1−p)−mp)

Words: 116 Articles: 1
Metapopulation OurBigBook.com
Colonization of empty habitat at rate c and extinction of occupied habitat at rate m give the displayed patch-occupancy equation. The positive equilibrium is 1−m/c when c>m. Competition can be incorporated through replacement fluxes between patches occupied by different species.

Colonization-competition tradeoff invasion fitness (f(y,x)=m[c(y)/c(x)−1]+[B(y)−B(x)][1−m/c(x)])

Words: 76
Levins metapopulation model OurBigBook.com
A resident trait x occupies fraction 1−m/c(x) when its colonization rate exceeds fire extinction. With net competitive replacement given by ability difference B(y)−B(x), a rare mutant has the displayed per-capita growth. The selection gradient is g(x)=mc′(x)/c(x)+[1−m/c(x)]B′(x). A singular trait with negative mutant-fitness curvature is a strict local evolutionarily stable strategy. Global strict uninvadability requires that mc(y)+[c(x)−m]B(y) be smaller than its resident value for every other trait. Monotonicity alone does not specify the shape or existence of an optimum.

Allee effect

Words: 46
Mathematical biology OurBigBook.com
An Allee effect makes per-capita growth less favorable at low abundance. A strong effect permits a stable zero state and a stable positive state separated by a finite threshold. Cooperative infections can exhibit the same positive-feedback structure: neither disease invades alone, but sufficiently many joint infections sustain both.

Food web

Words: 219 Articles: 3
Mathematical biology OurBigBook.com
A food web records resource-consumer interactions among species. A linear food chain is a special case. Positive interaction coefficients alone do not imply persistence: the per-capita growth balances must admit feasible positive long-term mean abundances.

Competitive exclusion principle

Words: 73
Food web OurBigBook.com
Two consumers with different break-even requirements cannot both have bounded persistent abundance on a single well-mixed limiting resource when their per-capita growth is linear in that resource. For Y˙/Y=cX−d and Z˙/Z=eX−f, differentiation of logY/c−logZ/e gives the nonzero constant −d/c+f/e when their break-even levels differ. This excludes simultaneous bounded persistence without assuming convergence to an equilibrium. Additional resources, environmental variation or different interactions can invalidate the simple one-resource argument.

Food chain

Words: 116 Articles: 1
Food web OurBigBook.com
A food chain orders species so that each consumer feeds on the level below and may be eaten by the level above. Basal resource growth, consumer mortality, conversion efficiency and density regulation determine whether all levels can persist.

Lotka-Volterra food-chain parity (N even: invertible interaction matrix; N odd: compatibility condition)

Words: 80
Food chain OurBigBook.com
For an unregulated exponential basal resource and nearest-neighbor Lotka-Volterra equations, the weighted interaction matrix is skew-symmetric matrix. An even chain has an invertible tridiagonal interaction matrix; its positive equilibrium, when feasible, fixes all long-term means. An odd chain has a null direction and requires a special balance between resource growth and mortality to permit bounded full coexistence. For a three-level chain, X1b2​​X3a1​​=Cexp[(b2​r−a1​d3​)t]. A positive even-chain equilibrium gives a conserved coercive relative-entropy-type function, proving every species remains bounded above and away from zero.

Gene regulatory network

Words: 377 Articles: 4
Mathematical biology OurBigBook.com
A network describing how gene products affect the production of other gene products. Positive and negative regulatory interactions can generate multistability, oscillations, and noise-sensitive transitions.

Mutual repression (x˙=f(y)−x,y˙​=g(x)−y)

Words: 349 Articles: 3
Gene regulatory network OurBigBook.com
Two components mutually repress when each inhibits the other's production. With decreasing f,g, the two negative interactions create a positive feedback loop. Sufficiently strong repression can produce two stable states: high x, low y, and the reverse.
// Target: mathematical-biology.bigb

Common-strength Hill repression criterion (maxKm,n​>1)

Words: 107
Mutual repression OurBigBook.com
For x˙=λ/(1+ym)−x, y˙​=λ/(1+xn)−y, the equilibrium slope product is K=mnxnym/[(1+xn)(1+ym)]. A value K>1 gives a saddle separating attracting alternatives. Both exponents greater than one allow this at sufficiently large common λ. If both are at most one it is impossible. If 0<m≤1<n, define Y(x) as the unique positive solution of Y−1+Ym−1=x−1+xn−1 and set Km,n​(x)=mnxnY(x)m/[(1+xn)(1+Y(x)m)]. All equilibria are parameterized by λ=x(1+Ym), whose derivative is (1+Ym)(1−K)/(1−mYm/(1+Ym)). Thus multistability for some common strength occurs exactly when maxx>0​Km,n​(x)>1. For m=1 the maximum is (n−1)2[(n+1)/(n−1)](n+1)/n/(4n). Consequently mn>1 alone is not sufficient when the two synthesis strengths are required to coincide.

Equal-strength power-law mutual repression (f(y)=λ(1+y)−n,g(x)=λ(1+x)−m)

Words: 125
Mutual repression OurBigBook.com
For positive m,n, this mutual repression system can display bistability for some λ exactly when both m>1 and n>1. If either exponent is at most one, it has a unique stable equilibrium for every λ. To prove the less obvious case m≤1<n, put a=x/(1+x) and b=y/(1+y) at equilibrium. Equality of the two expressions for λ gives a≤b(1−b)n−1. The loop gain is then bounded by mnb2(1−b)n−1, whose maximum is 4mn(n−1)n−1/(n+1)n+1<1. Swap the two components for the other case. If both exponents exceed one, sufficiently large λ yields two stable equilibria with (x,y)∼(λ,λ1−m) and (x,y)∼(λ1−n,λ).
